title: Donkey Water · Night Post
author: A text game in Watson Hartsoe’s Donkey Water / Ahiya Area Network

west.name: Western Basin
west.intro: June knows where the bride loses her shoe. Her mother left the camera running afterward. There are eight more seconds on the hill master. June wants to hear them.
west.opening: June’s wedding film ends when the bride drops her shoe. “Mum left the camera running,” she says, winding one earphone around her thumb. Mistletoe waits under the cold pump.
west.publicDesc: The bride steps off the ferry. A shoe falls through the boards. In the front row the bride, now an old woman, raises her own foot a second before it happens.
west.privateDesc: A thumbnail against a latch. A breath close to the microphone. A laugh from farther down the ferry. June turns her phone face down to listen again.
west.returnDesc: Tess takes June’s correction. The catalog now names Ruth as camera operator. A separate space stays open for the voice at the end.
west.permissionText: Etta signs two slips. The yard may see the wedding through the falling shoe. June may keep the last eight seconds on her own phone. Etta offers to witness the household claim as well.
west.coolText: Tess takes nine liters on the clean side of the exchanger. The inner rack comes up. Ruth’s reel appears under a blank maker’s name.
west.dockText: The dock keeps the family tail separate from the public edit. Two slips travel under the same can strap. Tess seals the cap before Imani lifts it.
tailWords: A thumbnail finds the camera latch.
A second laugh comes from down the boards.
west.replyLine: “Put down that she made the picture. Leave a space for who was laughing.”
west.storyEnd: Ruth is credited on the next yard print. The voice on the last eight seconds remains for the family to name.

ahiya.name: Ahiya Highlands
ahiya.publicTitle: The verse with a live answer
ahiya.returnTitle: A second harmony from the yard
ahiya.intro: Rahel can tell her cousin’s recording by a chair scraping just before the first note. Her aunt wants the three rehearsal takes back. She will sing the answer herself if the compound gives her a night.
ahiya.opening: Saba unties the chalk from the lower pump. Rahel wants the rehearsal her cousin recorded on the far side of the ridge. She knows the take by the sound of a chair scraping before the first note.
ahiya.publicDesc: Her aunt sings the answer in the flesh while the approved backing plays from the root bowl. Someone catches the wrong-key entrance and sings it back. The whole yard knows that take.
ahiya.privateDesc: Rahel passes her aunt the earphone. In the third take a chair scrapes stone. She knows at once which cousin sat where. The aunt keeps a listening copy on her own phone.
ahiya.returnDesc: The hill keeper files the aunt’s new answer beside the cousin’s first take. Both names stay with the rehearsal, and only their households receive the listening copies.
ahiya.permissionText: At the white wall the aunt grants household listening. She will allow the backing at one public performance if she can sing the answer there herself.
ahiya.coolText: The hill keeper opens the inner rack. Nine liters pass into the clean cooling branch. Three versions of the same verse turn up in the catalog.
ahiya.dockText: The hill keeper writes the listening takes and the permitted backing to the saddle water. The sealed lacquer label names the aunt as custodian.
tailWords: A chair leg scrapes the floor.
A cousin comes in early on the held note.
The aunt hums a second line over the first.
ahiya.replyLine: “Keep the wrong one too. That’s the only one where we all came in together.”
ahiya.storyEnd: Two versions of the harmony can now come home. A future public performance will need the aunt’s leave again.

overlook.name: Overlook Wellhead
overlook.summary: The pump keeper has chalked a white line across the can. Four liters belong to the animal and the return.
overlook.look: The casting says HAND PUMP. Somebody has scratched two smaller words into the handle. BOTH WAYS. A girl in the yard is holding a cup in exactly the way grown people hold a microphone.
overlook.caption: Mistletoe at the lower pump

switchback.name: Moraine Switchback Cistern
switchback.summary: A wooden trough sits in the lee of the bluff. The relief keeper has hung the resting animals’ names beside the wage book.
switchback.look: A mended saddle pad is drying inside out. From the cut in the road you can make out five loops of perforated film against the lighter pines. A stallholder chalks the price of meal onto a box.
switchback.caption: The pack-frame repair yard

ford.name: Silver Ford Relay
ford.summary: Etta keeps the key to the wedding master on a length of cotton. She is sitting where the old ferry rope once met the bank.
ford.look: One ferryman points to the wet post. His brother points to a stone some distance away. From the camera’s height the two landmarks line up. An enamel bowl has taken root on the island.
ford.caption: The landing below the survey camera

oxbow.name: Cottonwood Oxbow Kiosk
oxbow.summary: Two sheets hang at different depths. The cup, the root bowl and June’s phone all wait on the same bench.
oxbow.look: Etta bound a damaged reel along a young cottonwood shoot. Three wet seasons later the shoot put out a leaf with square holes along its edge. A baker has a price slip for the far bank.
oxbow.caption: The public sheet and the family awning

plaza.name: Highland Pueblo Plaza
plaza.summary: Tess can see the coolant gauge in the reflection of June’s empty cup. The archive dock and the household tap face the same line.
plaza.look: Behind the wire glass, a hose knocks twice. The registrar has a line for a deed holder. She keeps the rest of the page blank for guardians who bring their own witness.
plaza.caption: Public water and the archive intake

fluke.name: Whale Fluke Cistern
fluke.summary: The roofs give way to the ribs of a wreck. Between them the projectionist stretches a strip of cloth wide enough for two endings.
fluke.look: Two screenings went out on the tide. Both poles kept their seats. The film keeper has a comedy in two captions and two wooden chairs for people who remember the joke differently.
fluke.caption: Film drying between the ribs

apron.name: Half Dome East Apron
apron.summary: A second licensed pump draws from a narrow seep. A retired keeper wants the missing angle of a brass float recorded.
apron.look: The keeper can free the float with half a turn of her wrist. In the old film her sleeve covers her hand. She has left a flat place on the shelf for a new camera.
apron.caption: The east pump and the granite shelf

tetons.name: Teton Range Landing
tetons.summary: The survey cairn throws a short shadow. The road below bends out of sight well before the next gleam of water.
tetons.look: On the roof deck the tripod holes sit under the saddle cradle. Looking down, you can count three valleys by the turns a carrier would have to make. The cairn holds a dry dispatch box.
tetons.caption: Woody and Mistletoe above the pass

basalt.name: Basalt Pump
basalt.summary: Saba listens for the short stroke before she opens the valve. A clean line of chalk marks the well’s reserve.
basalt.look: The wind between pump strokes sounds like somebody breathing in to sing. In the handle’s shadow a piece of thread marks the height of the last entirely public draw.
basalt.caption: Rahel meets the pack below the ridge

beacon.name: Cross-Beacon Watch
beacon.summary: The congregation lends its high wall to the watch. Different people give the beam different names.
beacon.look: Rahel’s aunt has folded a rehearsal sheet into her pocket. She lets people hear an early entrance in the wrong key if they will listen to what the other singer did next.
beacon.caption: The ridge above the night convoy

hill.name: Hill Archive
hill.summary: One operator logs the crossing. Another clears a space on the shelf for the returning rehearsal. The fans carry on between sightings.
hill.look: A map can tell the operator where a can was seen. To learn who sang the lower voice she needs a recording and someone who knows the family. Saba’s signed gauge reading lies under the keyboard.
hill.caption: The radio desk at the hill master

compound.name: Daylight Compound
compound.summary: Two people take the handles before the pack frame comes away. The phones go dark in the direct morning sun.
compound.look: A clay bowl sits beside the household tap. There is a stool for a singer under the awning. Somebody has pegged an ordinary sheet between the walls for tonight’s backing reel.
compound.caption: The unloading yard at first light

groves.name: Overlook Rim Film Grove
groves.program: The pump keeper’s first test roll

groves.name: Moraine Bench Ribbon Wood
groves.program: Two cuts of the same thaw

groves.name: Cottonwood Oxbow Film Forest
groves.program: A double bill chosen by the yard

groves.name: Galleon Arch Kelp Cinema
groves.program: A comedy dubbed on two shores

groves.name: Half Dome Cloud Notch Stand
groves.program: A pilot’s cloud and shadow tests

groves.name: Half Dome East Apron Forest
groves.program: The same cliff in three prints

people: A western saddle mechanic and June’s guardian. She hears a split in the pack frame before she sees water at the seam.
Ruth’s daughter. She wants to hear the end of her mother’s film and decide what can be played outside the family.
Print keeper at Silver Ford. She can license the wedding and witness June’s household claim.
Cooling operator at the plaza. She records public water and rack water on two different slips.
Keeper of the basalt pump. She can close the intake even when the remote map shows a full tank.
Sound runner on the night route. She knows the singers by the chairs they move before a take.
Custodian of three rehearsal takes. She can grant listening at home and sing a single public answer in person.
A living carrier. The wet saddle keeps the recording legible in motion, including on Woody’s roof. Her western namesake traveled into the Sierra with Ansel Adams and Francis Holman.
law: A live can holds up to 20 L. A donkey keeps its moving recording in order. A dry can loses its traveling copies. An approved recording saved on its recipient’s phone survives.

A routine draw stops at the well’s reserve. An emergency draw below the line closes that well for at least two local shift changes and until its level recovers. Cisterns receive water. Only wells produce it.

The first four liters aboard are set aside for travel and animal care. Cooling, the public tap and the grove draw from the water above that mark. An explicit emergency release can empty the whole can.

Imani and Mistletoe fly together in Woody. A local flight drinks 1 L. A direct crossing to or from the far Teton landing drinks 2 L. Select a destination and then land. Roads remain passable on a dry return.

A shift has 18 watches. A road leg uses its posted time and one measure of strength per watch. Rest restores three strength. A drink from the can restores all six. At the last watch there is always a handoff, including a safe landing.
Time advances on the active circuit. Switching hands opens the other carrier’s log at their own stop. Wells, people, letters and saddle water stay where they were.
A custodian grants the cut for the public sheet and the take for a named listener. The private recording stays under the awning. A credit or correction travels in a wet can back to the original rack.

Adams’s Sierra pack burro and roof-mounted camera deck return in the fictional flying Woody. A field plate records the maker, stop and exposure zone. A film tree can show a local plate once it is awake.
storyGrammar: LOOK
Read the place, its witnesses and available equipment. Reading a room costs no time.
PUMP / OVERDRAW
Fill at a marked well. An emergency draw has a separate confirmation and a lasting cost.
GO <stop>
Walk a connected road with the animal and the live cargo.
TAKE OFF / FLY <stop> / LAND
Lift off in Woody in the west, commit the wet travel cost, then land with the donkey and the can.
ASK / COOL / COPY
See the custodian, fund the clean rack branch, then dock the saddle and take the licensed cuts.
WATER / REST / TAP
Water the animal, rest at a stop or allocate water to households.
AERIAL / SCREEN / LISTEN / FILE
Wake local film trees, exhibit only the licensed cut, leave the household copy on its recipient’s phone and return the correction.
EXPOSE / PROJECT
Make a field plate and hang it on a frond where a projection is permitted.
MAP / JOURNAL / BOOK
Read the atlas, turn transcript or worldtext. Each view preserves the active place.
HANDOFF / SWITCH
Close the local watch or take up the other circuit. The well remembers what was drawn.

west.name: The baker’s price slip
west.ask: Nell needs the current meal price before she bakes tomorrow’s order.
west.reply: Six measures a sack, marked with this morning’s date.
west.delivered: Nell writes the dated price on her flour bin. The chalk survives after the can is empty.

ahiya.name: Three sounds from one room
ahiya.ask: The children challenge the ridge crew to name a rasping sound.
ahiya.reply: The ridge team guesses a cooling fan. Rahel’s cousin wagers it was a spoon on a washboard.
ahiya.delivered: The children turn over a washboard and laugh. They set aside three sounds for the next run.
